accuracy.evidence: Shape facts checked against the DfE Year 1 and Year 2 programmes of study and CCSS 1.G.A.2: a cube has 6 congruent square faces, a cuboid (right rectangular prism) has 6 rectangular faces, a cylinder has 2 flat circular faces and a curved surface, a cone has 1 flat circular face, a curved surface and an apex. 2 or 3 unit cubes in a row form a cuboid (not a cube, since length differs from height); 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 unit cubes form a cube, built as 4 + 4 in two layers. Parameterised answers a+1, a+b and 4*a are whole numbers at every corner of their ranges.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips NCETM notes for Year 1-2 3-D shape work: using flat names for solids (circle and triangle tiles are traps in 'Name the parts', the pencil-tip prediction, robot saying 2, challenge 'flat', p3, m3), calling 2 joined cubes a bigger cube (cube-scene prediction, robot saying 3, challenge 'two', p4), counting only visible cubes (the 2x2x2 build hides a cube at the back, challenge 'hidden', m2, m8) and stacking on the point of a cone (plan-scene prediction, the build refuses with a reason, robot saying 4, challenge 'point', p5).

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab composes solids into new solids: stack parts in order to copy a plan card, name each highlighted part of a composite model, and fill dashed cube spaces to see a cuboid and a 2x2x2 cube form. flagsolid (468) turns one solid to count faces, flagtower (304) tests balance and bridge spans, and flagcompose (739) joins flat pattern blocks; none builds or decomposes a 3-D composite. The lab_distinct gate keeps flag_solidbuild.js under 30% similar to every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers by building: the plan card only accepts the right part in order, and a wrong tap names the shape tapped and how to spot the one needed ('A cylinder has a curved side and a flat circle at each end'). In the cube scene the cube count ticks up, a hint says 'Now start the top layer' at 4, and the finished shape is held on screen with 'You made a cuboid!' or 'a bigger cube', so the new name comes from the shape they built.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'Could the cone go at the bottom, under a cylinder?' (Yes; the build refuses anything on a cone point), 'What shape is the sharp end of a pencil?' (A triangle; the pencil model's tip must be named cone) and 'Push 2 cubes together, end to end. What new shape?' (A bigger cube; the first build makes a cuboid). Step completion reveals the child's own prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with two tagged wrong answers each. why() has six distinct messages: flat (circles and triangles are flat, solids have 3-D names), two (2 long but 1 tall is a cuboid), point (nothing sits on a cone point), roll (a ball rolls, a flat face goes at the bottom), hidden (count the hidden cubes: 4 + 4 = 8) and one (each part is its own shape).

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and concrete objects (tin, party hat, box, dice) and pass the family kid limit; the adult text names composite shape, cuboid, cylinder, cone and face, cites CCSS 1.G.A.2 and the Year 1-2 programme and passes the adult limit. Canvas words are dark on white labels, and every tile shows a picture plus the word.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph does one job: what a model is, the 3-D name of each part, why flat names are wrong, and which parts hold others plus cubes making cuboids and cubes. The adult text gives the standards and key words, what composing involves, four named mistakes, and exactly what the lab does. The content gate found no filler and under 12% overlap with every other lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark theme, at rest and part-way through each Show me: plan card and build area side by side above four tiles about 80 x 85 px each with a picture and name; six naming tiles in a 3 x 2 grid; the 8-cube build fits with all dashed spaces visible; Right and Slip are half-width cards about 75 px tall; nothing is clipped, and the pile label no longer overlaps the cube pile after the fix.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin under the canvas ('Put a cylinder on top', 'This part is a cone', 'Add one small cube to the model', 'Take the top part off your model', 'The robot made a slip'), each 56 px tall in the young style. Every change is spoken through c.say and set as the canvas aria-label; challenge feedback is a polite live region. Right and wrong use ticks, crosses and words, not colour alone. The walk gate's axe run is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
